sections.title: Texts read aloud
sections.intro: Finite works, narrated. A first episode and a last one, so you can work through them the way you would a book.

items.title: The Collected Teachings of Ajahn Chah: Audiobook
items.author: Read by Ajahn Amaro, Amaravati Buddhist Monastery
items.description: The complete collection of Ajahn Chah's talks in English, read in full during the winter of 2012. Two of the printed volumes, [Bodhinyana](reading.html#return-bodhinyana) and [Everything Is Teaching Us](reading.html#talk-1-everything-is-teaching-us), are on the reading shelf.

items.title: The Forest Path Podcast
items.author: Sol Hanna, Everyday Dhamma Network
items.description: Narrated translations of forest tradition teachers, much of it material that exists in English as text but rarely as audio. A good companion to the [Lives shelf](reading.html#lives).

items.title: Wisdom of the Masters
items.author: Samaneri Jayasara
items.description: Readings from teachers across several traditions: Buddhist, Advaita, Christian mystical, Sufi. Narrated slowly, closer to a contemplative recording than a talk. The widest net on this page and the least Theravada.

sections.title: From the monasteries
sections.intro: Places rather than single voices. Talks given to whoever was sitting there that evening.

items.title: Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery
items.author: Ajahn Pasanno and the sangha, Redwood Valley, California
items.description: Talks from the resident sangha and visiting teachers, recorded much as they were given. The video and audio archives do not overlap completely, so it is worth checking both.

items.title: Amaravati Buddhist Monastery
items.author: Amaravati Buddhist Monastery, Hertfordshire, England
items.description: Dhamma talks from the monastery Ajahn Sumedho founded in 1984. The audio library also holds separate collections of his talks and of recorded readings, so the library page is the better door than any single feed. His books are on the [reading shelf](reading.html#teachings-talks).

items.title: Aruna Ratanagiri
items.author: Ajahn Munindo and the sangha, Northumberland, England
items.description: Talks from Ajahn Munindo, unhurried even by the standards of this page. The monastery publishes its own feed; the Apple listing that circulates elsewhere points at a dead address and stopped updating in 2025.

items.title: Cittaviveka, Chithurst Buddhist Monastery
items.author: The sangha at Chithurst, West Sussex, England
items.description: The first of the English forest monasteries, established in 1979. Quieter and less frequently posted than Amaravati, which suits it.

items.title: Clear Mountain Monastery
items.author: Clear Mountain Monastery, greater Seattle
items.description: Talks and question sessions from an aspiring forest monastery, recorded while the community is still being established. That gives it a different texture from the older places above: more questions, fewer settled answers.

items.title: Wat Marp Jan
items.author: Ajahn Anan Akiñcano and the sangha, Rayong, Thailand
items.description: A forest monastery founded by a disciple of Ajahn Chah. Some material is in Thai without translation, so this is the one entry here where you may have to hunt.
items.meta: Thai forest, Thailand · talks, some untranslated

items.title: Evening talks by Thanissaro Bhikkhu
items.author: Metta Forest Monastery, California
items.description: Evening talks given before the sit, on mindfulness, concentration and the shape of the path. Most run about twelve minutes, which makes them the easiest thing on this page to fit into a day.
items.note: If you want somewhere to start: about twelve minutes each, and they ask little of you.

items.title: Ajahn Brahm
items.author: Ajahn Brahm, remastered by Everyday Dhamma Network
items.description: Older talks cleaned up and reissued rather than new recordings. The register is warmer and funnier than most of this page, carried by stories, which some people find is exactly the way in and others do not.
items.meta: Free · about an hour · [in podcast apps](https://pod.link/1651126858)

items.title: Yuttadhammo Bhikkhu
items.author: Bhante Yuttadhammo, Sirimangalo International
items.description: Practice instruction and live question sessions in the Mahasi method as taught in the Ajahn Tong lineage, which is the tradition behind [The Only Way](reading.html#meditation-the-only-way-path-to-nibbana) on the reading shelf and the centre at [Wat Chom Tong](places.html#wat-chom-tong). He answers ordinary questions directly, which is rarer than it should be.
items.meta: Mahasi, Ajahn Tong lineage · instruction and questions · [sirimangalo.org](https://sirimangalo.org/)

items.title: Ajahn Achalo Bhikkhu
items.author: Ajahn Achalo, Anandagiri Forest Monastery, Thailand
items.description: Step-by-step guided meditations alongside sutta readings and talks. Built as a plain, usable resource rather than a polished production, which is the reason to use it.
items.meta: Thai forest · guided sits and talks

items.title: Ajahn Sona
items.author: Ajahn Sona, Birken Forest Buddhist Monastery, British Columbia
items.description: Long-form talks that take their time and assume you will too. Among the most carefully argued teaching coming out of the Western forest sangha.

sections.title: The insight tradition
sections.intro: Outside the Thai forest lineage. Both come by way of Mahasi Sayadaw.

items.title: Insight Hour with Joseph Goldstein
items.author: Joseph Goldstein, Be Here Now Network
items.description: A long series working through the Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta passage by passage, with retreat talks alongside it. Worth knowing before you start: unlike everything else here it is a commercial production and carries advertising.
items.meta: Free with ads · about an hour · [in podcast apps](https://pod.link/1017103666)

items.title: Mindfulness Insight Meditation: Buddhist Teachings
items.author: Sayar Myat, Satipatthana Meditation Society of Canada
items.description: Talks and practice instruction in satipaṭṭhāna vipassanā following Mahasi Sayadaw's method, with more time given to instruction than most of this page.

sections.title: A first look
sections.intro: What I would send someone who asked a question and meant it.

items.title: Buddha Speaks
items.author: Anonymous channel, plain-English explainers
items.description: Short explanations of core teachings, kept simple without being vague. A good place to send someone just starting out, and not a deep well for anyone else.

items.title: Tergar Meditation Community
items.author: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
items.description: Meditation instruction built around the Joy of Living curriculum. Tibetan in lineage, taught in plain and often funny language that leans on modern science as much as on tradition. The most structured way in on this page.

sections.title: Study, and other traditions
sections.intro: Working through the texts themselves, and two voices from further afield.

items.title: The Buddha's Teaching As It Is
items.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi, Washington Buddhist Vihara, 1979
items.description: Ten lectures on the fundamentals of early Buddhism, given nearly fifty years ago and still the clearest sustained account I know of. His anthology [In the Buddha's Words](reading.html#early-in-the-buddha-s-words) is on the reading shelf.
items.meta: Early Buddhism · ten lectures · re-uploaded archive; [audio at Bodhi Monastery](https://bodhimonastery.org/online-dharma-lectures)

items.title: Metta Meditation, Santi Forest Monastery 2007
items.author: Bhante Sujato, ten talks, uploaded by Samita ASBL
items.description: Ten talks from a rains retreat in New South Wales, working through metta practice in more detail than almost anything else available. The translations used across [Reflections](reflections.html) are Bhante Sujato's.
items.meta: Thai forest · ten talks · re-uploaded archive, not an official channel

items.title: Doug's Dharma
items.author: Doug Smith, early Buddhism with a secular framing
items.description: Short videos relating early Buddhist teaching to ordinary life, from a scholarly angle rather than a devotional one. Useful for the same reason it is limited: it stays outside the practice looking in.
items.meta: Early Buddhism, secular framing · short videos

items.title: James Low
items.author: James Low, Dzogchen in the Nyingma tradition
items.description: A different tradition from the rest of this page, and the least introductory thing on it. Recorded seminars rather than talks, worth the time regardless of lineage.
